system_description.narrative_title: China's strategic control over tech, minerals and markets
system_description.narrative_summary: Headlines show Beijing increasingly using regulatory, commercial and diplomatic levers to consolidate control over advanced technology, critical minerals and domestic capital markets while foreign firms and governments respond by rerouting supply chains, blocking deals, and seeking alternative sources. The tussle is driving market volatility, deal casualties, and nascent de‑coupling in semiconductors, AI hardware and cleantech supply chains, with implications for geopolitics, investment flows and the global climate transition.
system_description.scope: State-led Chinese actions (export/import controls, deal approvals, overseas mining investments, regulatory and legal measures), corporate and investor responses (deal cancellations/blocks, supply‑chain reconfiguration, relocation of production and investment), market and financial signals (stock interventions, listings halts, investor flows), and bilateral/multilateral diplomatic and security reactions reported in the November 4–6, 2026 headlines.
system_description.super_system: The global geopolitical‑economic order: US–China strategic competition embedded in globalized technology, finance and climate transition systems.
adjacent_subsystems: Global semiconductor and AI hardware supply chain
Critical minerals and cleantech supply chain
Diplomatic and security/military relations among great powers

variables.name: Regulatory intervention intensity
variables.description: The overall frequency and severity of government regulatory actions that alter market access, corporate behavior, or technology operations.

variables.name: Export/import control stringency
variables.description: The strictness and scope of controls on the cross‑border movement of technologies, components and critical materials.

variables.name: Supply‑chain geographic concentration
variables.description: The degree to which production and inputs for key technologies and minerals are geographically concentrated in a limited set of locations.

variables.name: Supply‑chain rerouting rate
variables.description: The speed at which firms reconfigure sourcing and production footprints across regions in response to policy or market signals.

variables.name: Cross‑border investment flows
variables.description: Net volume and velocity of private and portfolio capital moving into or out of a jurisdiction’s technology and resource sectors.

variables.name: Critical‑mineral supply dependency
variables.description: The extent to which global or sectoral supply relies on a limited set of external sources for critical minerals.

variables.name: Domestic advanced technology capacity
variables.description: The depth and maturity of locally available capabilities for designing and producing advanced semiconductors, AI hardware and cleantech.

variables.name: Financial market volatility
variables.description: The amplitude and frequency of price swings and liquidity stress in equity, bond and currency markets relevant to the tech and resource sectors.

variables.name: Capital‑market openness
variables.description: The degree to which domestic capital markets permit foreign participation, listings and cross‑border capital operations.

variables.name: Deal approval and blocking intensity
variables.description: The propensity and rigor with which authorities scrutinize, approve, delay or block cross‑border mergers, acquisitions and investments.

variables.name: Investor confidence and risk perception
variables.description: Aggregate perceptions among domestic and foreign investors about regulatory, political and commercial risk in targeted sectors.

variables.name: Diplomatic and geopolitical tension
variables.description: The prevailing intensity of bilateral and multilateral political friction that affects trade, investment and security cooperation.

variables.name: Security‑framing of economic policy
variables.description: The extent to which national economic policy is explicitly justified or shaped by national security considerations.

variables.name: Rate of trade restriction adoption
variables.description: The velocity at which new tariffs, bans, screening rules or other trade barriers are introduced or tightened.

variables.name: International technology transfer rate
variables.description: The flow rate of know‑how, designs, skilled personnel and research outputs moving across borders, both formal and informal.

variables.name: Cleantech investment flows
variables.description: The volume and direction of capital specifically allocated to clean energy, electrification and related climate technologies.

catalysts.title: US Congressional briefing with Nvidia CEO
catalysts.description: US lawmakers are preparing briefings of Nvidia's CEO over China spying concerns; hearings could prompt new US export or disclosure measures affecting China access to AI chips.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'US lawmakers summon Jensen Huang', 'Key Republicans seek briefing from Nvidia CEO over Chinese spy allegations'

catalysts.title: APEC summit meetings and bilateral talks
catalysts.description: APEC leader- and minister-level meetings will produce negotiations and side talks affecting trade, investment and tech cooperation between China and regional partners.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'China’s tech megacity cleans up seedy underbelly for Apec summit' — summit will drive near-term diplomacy and trade signals

catalysts.title: Escalation of deal scrutiny and blocking (robotics/AI)
catalysts.description: China's recent block of SoftBank's ABB robotics takeover signals a continuing pattern of stricter scrutiny and blocking of foreign tech takeovers in strategic sectors.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'China Blocks $5.4 Billion SoftBank Robot Deal', 'China’s block on SoftBank deal fires the starting gun on the robot wars'

catalysts.title: China withholds import approvals for advanced chips
catalysts.description: Reports of Nvidia chips accumulating in Hong Kong as China withholds import approvals point to tighter import controls and selective access to advanced AI chips.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Nvidia chips pile up in Hong Kong as China withholds import approval', 'Nvidia orders data centre clients to reduce China exposure'

catalysts.title: China expands overseas mining stakes and partnerships
catalysts.description: China's accelerated overseas stakes and new mining partnerships (eg. Gabon) will strengthen its grip on critical minerals and overseas supply influence.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'China expands overseas mining stakes, tightening grip on critical minerals', 'China, Gabon elevate ties, pledge deeper mining...'

catalysts.title: Growth in non-China rare-earth supply deals
catalysts.description: Deals by companies like Solvay to source rare earths outside China signal a rising alternative supply chain that could modestly reduce global dependence on China.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Solvay strikes rare earths deal that will reduce global dependence on China'

catalysts.title: Chinese market support & listing halts
catalysts.description: Beijing's active interventions to prop up AI stocks and temporary halts of listings aim to stabilise markets but limit foreign access and transparency.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'China steps up defence of stock market', 'China halts listings', 'China’s Central Bank Tweaks Forex Reserve Rules'

catalysts.title: Push to build homegrown chip tooling and memory production
catalysts.description: Chinese flash memory leaders targeting homegrown tools and global makers considering memory plans indicate an industry push to localise advanced chip production and tooling.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'China's top flash memory chipmaker targets more homegrown tools', 'TSMC considers making advanced memory chips'

catalysts.title: US pressure to enforce Busan trade deal
catalysts.description: US warnings that China must 'immediately' meet Busan trade deal terms could trigger enforcement steps or retaliatory trade measures in the near term.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'US warns China it must ‘immediately’ meet terms of Busan trade deal'

catalysts.title: Firms accelerate supply and market rerouting away from China
catalysts.description: Actions by Nvidia, SK Hynix, Moonshot and others signal an intensifying corporate push to reroute sourcing, cloud access and investments away from China.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Nvidia orders data centre clients to reduce China exposure', 'SK Hynix's New York chip plans hit snag', 'Moonshot turned to Europe for Nvidia Blackwell access'
